newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu expected on surprise French Riviera trip.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu expected on surprise French Riviera trip.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko will return on Thursday to the French Riviera, where he convalesced from cancer treatment late last year, after spending less than a month in his chaotic country.

Mobutu, who reshuffled the government and the army command during his brief stay at home and vowed to crush rebels, was due to land at midday at Nice airport on a private flight, the office of the prefect (government representative) in the French Riviera capital said.
The duration and reasons for his surprise visit were not known. The official said he had been granted an open-ended French visa.
Mobutu returned home to Kinshasa from his palatial mansion in Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, near Nice, last December 17 as rebels made major territorial gains in eastern Zaire.
He had been away since last August, undergoing cancer surgery in Switzerland and later resting at his Riviera villa.
Returning to a triumphal welcome in Kinshasa, Mobutu appointed a crisis cabinet and named a new army chief, General Mahele Lieko Bokoungo, to try end the revolt in the east.
The rebels have thrust out from the North and South Kivu area they originally controlled and fighting has raged around the eastern town of Bunia in Upper Zaire.
The alliance that began the rebellion three months ago with a group of mostly ethnic Tutsis, now occupies a 500 km (300 mile) swath of eastern Zaire along the border with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda.
The rebels, led by longtime Mobutu opponent Laurent Kabila, have vowed to march to Kinshasa to overthrow Mobutu who has ruled the mineral-rich country for 31 years.
Mobutu has ruled out negotiation with Kabila and vowed to crush him. But analysts say Zaire is not in a position to inflict heavy losses on the better-equipped rebels.
Mobutu also faces trouble from the radical opposition, which says it no longer considers him as president and has vowed a wide-ranging campaign of civil disobedience to end his rule.
